title: Austin's Post-War Boom: Growth and Global Aid
summary:
Here's a summary of the Austin City Council meeting from May 16, 1946:

*   **Historic Infrastructure Investment:** Voters overwhelmingly approved nearly $18.2 million (equivalent to approximately $280 million today) in bonds. This massive funding package will support 14 major civic projects, including new schools, hospital improvements, street upgrades, a municipal auditorium, and expansions to the city's airport, fire stations, and utility systems (water, electric, sewer).
*   **Post-War Famine Relief:** A special Famine Committee was established to coordinate food collection efforts, responding to a government call for aid to starving populations in war-torn Europe and the Far East.
*   **Community Events & Development:** The American Legion received approval to host a three-day Fourth of July celebration at Zilker Park. Additionally, a special permit was granted for the construction of a new doctor's office and clinic.

Director of Public Works; R. D. Thorp, Chief of Police.
A letter was received from the Govalle Civic League approving the "Walker and Gibson
tracts of land" as the location for a park and recreation center. The Mayor stated that
this would be taken under consideration but the Council could not make a definite promise
that this land would be purchased for park purposes.
Mr. Ed Knebel, representing American Legion Post 76, appeared and requested permission for
the use of Zilker Park for a 3-day July 4th celebration by the American Legion this year.
The Mayor assured Mr. Knebel that the City would be glad to have the Legion use the Park
and sponsor this celebration, and would also be glad to assist the Legion in every way
possible during that time.
Mr. Daniels, representative of the U. S. Department of Agriculture, appeared and told
about the program the government is asking all cities thru out the nation to participate
in, and asked that the Mayor appoint a Famine Committee for Austin to take charge of the
collection of food to be sent to the starving people of Europe and the Far East. The Mayor
assured Mr. Daniels that the City would cooperate in every way possible in this very
worthy project.
